q: Tu vois Paul ? Oui, je ___ vois.
e: Do you see Paul? Yes, I see him.
w: A masculine direct object (no à) becomes le, placed before the verb.

q: Tu connais Julie ? Oui, je ___ connais.
e: Do you know Julie? Yes, I know her.
w: A feminine direct object (no à) becomes la, placed before the verb.

q: Tu aimes les fraises ? Oui, je ___ adore.
e: Do you like strawberries? Yes, I love them.
w: A plural direct object becomes les, whatever the gender; leur is only for à + people.

q: Tu prends le bus ? Oui, je ___ prends.
e: Are you taking the bus? Yes, I'm taking it.
w: A masculine direct object (no à) becomes le, placed before the verb.

q: Où est ma clé ? Je ne ___ trouve pas.
e: Where's my key? I can't find it.
w: Clé is feminine, so la; it sits between ne and the verb.

q: Tu regardes la télé ? Non, je ne ___ regarde pas.
e: Are you watching TV? No, I'm not watching it.
w: A feminine direct object (no à) becomes la, placed before the verb.

q: Vous avez les billets ? Oui, nous ___ avons.
e: Do you have the tickets? Yes, we have them.
w: A plural direct object becomes les, whatever the gender; leur is only for à + people.

q: Tu aimes ce film ? Oui, je ___ aime beaucoup.
e: Do you like this film? Yes, I really like it.
w: Le and la become l' before a vowel or a silent h.
wf: le devient l' devant une voyelle.

q: Tu manges ta soupe ? Oui, je ___ mange.
e: Are you eating your soup? Yes, I'm eating it.
w: A feminine direct object (no à) becomes la, placed before the verb.

q: Tu écoutes la radio ? Oui, je ___ écoute.
e: Do you listen to the radio? Yes, I listen to it.
w: Écouter takes a direct object, and la becomes l' before a vowel.

q: Il appelle ses parents ? Oui, il ___ appelle.
e: Is he calling his parents? Yes, he's calling them.
w: Appeler takes a direct object: appeler quelqu'un, so les, not leur.

q: Elle invite Marc ? Oui, elle ___ invite.
e: Is she inviting Marc? Yes, she's inviting him.
w: Inviter takes a direct object; le becomes l' before a vowel.

q: Tu fais tes devoirs ? Oui, je ___ fais maintenant.
e: Are you doing your homework? Yes, I'm doing it now.
w: Devoirs is plural in French, so les.

q: Le café, tu ___ veux avec du sucre ?
e: The coffee, do you want it with sugar?
w: A masculine direct object (no à) becomes le, placed before the verb.

q: Ces chaussures, je ___ achète !
e: These shoes, I'm buying them!
w: A plural direct object becomes les, whatever the gender; leur is only for à + people.

q: Tu connais l'adresse ? Non, je ne ___ connais pas.
e: Do you know the address? No, I don't know it.
w: Adresse is feminine, so la, between ne and the verb.

q: Tu bois ton café ? Oui, je ___ bois.
e: Are you drinking your coffee? Yes, I'm drinking it.
w: A masculine direct object (no à) becomes le, placed before the verb.

q: Tu lis le journal ? Oui, je ___ lis tous les matins.
e: Do you read the paper? Yes, I read it every morning.
w: A masculine direct object (no à) becomes le, placed before the verb.

q: Vous voyez la mer ? Oui, on ___ voit d'ici.
e: Can you see the sea? Yes, you can see it from here.
w: A feminine direct object (no à) becomes la, placed before the verb.

q: Tes parents ? Je ___ vois le dimanche.
e: Your parents? I see them on Sundays.
w: Voir takes a direct object, so les for people too, not leur.

q: Tu cherches ton téléphone ? Je ___ ai vu sur la table.
e: Looking for your phone? I saw it on the table.
w: In the passé composé the pronoun goes before avoir, and le or la becomes l'.
wf: Au passé composé : je l'ai vu.

q: La lettre ? Je ___ ai écrite hier.
e: The letter? I wrote it yesterday.
w: In the passé composé the pronoun goes before avoir, and le or la becomes l'.
wf: Au passé composé : je l'ai écrite.

q: Les clés ? Je ___ ai laissées dans la voiture.
e: The keys? I left them in the car.
w: Les goes before avoir, and the participle agrees: laissées.

q: Ton frère ? Je ne ___ ai pas vu.
e: Your brother? I haven't seen him.
w: Ne goes before the pronoun and avoir: je ne l'ai pas vu.

q: Sophie ? Je vais ___ appeler ce soir.
e: Sophie? I'm going to call her tonight.
w: With a verb plus infinitive, the pronoun goes just before the infinitive.

q: Ce livre, tu peux ___ lire ce week-end.
e: This book, you can read it this weekend.
w: With a verb plus infinitive, the pronoun goes just before the infinitive.

q: Mes lunettes ? Je ne peux pas ___ trouver.
e: My glasses? I can't find them.
w: With a verb plus infinitive, the pronoun goes just before the infinitive.

q: La fenêtre ? Ouvre-___, s'il te plaît.
e: The window? Open it, please.
w: In a positive command the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen: ouvre-la.

q: Tes devoirs ? Fais-___ tout de suite !
e: Your homework? Do it right now!
w: In a positive command the pronoun follows the verb: fais-les.

q: Le gâteau ? Ne ___ mange pas tout !
e: The cake? Don't eat all of it!
w: In a negative command the pronoun goes back before the verb: ne le mange pas.
wf: Impératif négatif : ne le mange pas.

q: Cette chanson, je ___ écoute en boucle.
e: I listen to this song on repeat.
w: Chanson is feminine; la becomes l' before a vowel.
wf: la devient l' devant une voyelle.

q: Tu as fini le rapport ? Oui, je ___ ai fini.
e: Have you finished the report? Yes, I've finished it.
w: In the passé composé the pronoun goes before avoir, and le or la becomes l'.
wf: Au passé composé : je l'ai fini.

q: Ces fleurs, c'est Marie qui ___ a choisies.
e: These flowers, Marie chose them.
w: Les comes before avoir, and choisies agrees with it.

q: Ma voiture, je ___ ai vendue l'année dernière.
e: My car, I sold it last year.
w: La becomes l' before avoir; vendue agrees with the feminine object.

q: Le film ? Je viens de ___ voir.
e: The film? I've just seen it.
w: After venir de, the pronoun goes before the infinitive: je viens de le voir.

q: Ce travail, je ne veux pas ___ faire seul.
e: I don't want to do this job alone.
w: With a verb plus infinitive, the pronoun goes just before the infinitive.

q: Les enfants ? Je ___ ai entendus rentrer.
e: The children? I heard them come home.
w: Entendre takes a direct object; les goes before avoir and entendus agrees.

q: Tes parents, il faut ___ prévenir avant midi.
e: Your parents, you need to let them know before noon.
w: Prévenir takes a direct object: prévenir quelqu'un, so les.

q: Claire ? Je ___ ai attendue une heure !
e: Claire? I waited an hour for her!
w: Attendre takes a direct object in French (no for), so l', not lui.

q: Ton chef ? Tu dois ___ écouter.
e: Your boss? You have to listen to him.
w: Écouter takes a direct object (no to), so l', not lui.

q: Les voisins ? Je ___ aide souvent.
e: The neighbours? I often help them.
w: Aider takes a direct object: aider quelqu'un, so les, not leur.

q: Ta grand-mère ? Je ___ remercie pour le cadeau.
e: Your grandmother? I'm thanking her for the present.
w: Remercier takes a direct object: remercier quelqu'un, so la, not lui.

q: Le prof ? On ___ a cherché partout.
e: The teacher? We looked for him everywhere.
w: Chercher takes a direct object (no for), so l'.

q: Ta sœur ? Je ___ ai rencontrée à Lyon.
e: Your sister? I met her in Lyon.
w: La becomes l' before avoir; rencontrée agrees with it.

q: Les résultats, on ne ___ connaît pas encore.
e: We don't know the results yet.
w: A plural direct object becomes les, whatever the gender; leur is only for à + people.

q: Cette robe, je ___ trouve très jolie.
e: I think this dress is really pretty.
w: Trouver + object + adjective: the object pronoun is la.

q: Ton dossier, je ___ ai transmis au directeur.
e: Your file, I passed it on to the director.
w: In the passé composé the pronoun goes before avoir, and le or la becomes l'.
wf: Au passé composé : je l'ai transmis.

q: La vérité, il faut ___ dire.
e: The truth, you have to tell it.
w: With a verb plus infinitive, the pronoun goes just before the infinitive.

q: Ces erreurs, je ___ ai faites sans le vouloir.
e: I made these mistakes without meaning to.
w: Les goes before avoir, and faites agrees with it.

q: Tu savais qu'il part ? Oui, je ___ savais.
e: Did you know he's leaving? Yes, I knew.
w: Le can stand for a whole idea or clause: je le savais.

q: Elle est fatiguée ? Oui, elle ___ est.
e: Is she tired? Yes, she is.
w: Le stands for an adjective after être, with no agreement: elle l'est.

q: Tu crois qu'il viendra ? Je ne ___ crois pas.
e: Do you think he'll come? I don't think so.
w: Neutral le stands for the clause: je ne le crois pas, I don't think so.
wf: le neutre : je ne le crois pas.

q: Il est plus riche qu'on ne ___ pense.
e: He's richer than people think.
w: Comparisons often take a neutral le for the idea: qu'on ne le pense.

q: La maison, ils ___ ont fait construire.
e: The house, they had it built.
w: With faire + infinitive the pronoun goes before faire; fait never agrees.

q: Ton vélo ? Je ___ fais réparer demain.
e: Your bike? I'm having it repaired tomorrow.
w: With faire + infinitive the pronoun goes before faire: je le fais réparer.

q: Les enfants, je ___ laisse jouer dehors.
e: I let the children play outside.
w: With laisser + infinitive the pronoun goes before laisser: je les laisse jouer.

q: Comme je te ___ ai dit, la réunion est annulée.
e: As I told you, the meeting is cancelled.
w: Neutral le stands for what was said: comme je te l'ai dit.
wf: le neutre : comme je te l'ai dit.

q: Venez demain si vous ___ voulez.
e: Come tomorrow if you like.
w: Neutral le can stand for an idea: si vous le voulez.

q: Elle est médecin, et sa fille ___ deviendra aussi.
e: She's a doctor, and her daughter will become one too.
w: Neutral le stands for a role after devenir or être, with no agreement.

q: Cette solution, je ___ juge trop risquée.
e: I consider this solution too risky.
w: Juger + object + adjective: la for a feminine noun.
